Needs changes before merge.

The forward and inverse tests cover offsets, rotary signs, travel limits, and pole crossings. The change has no new dependency, UI change, or changed golden file.

Local results, with upstream/main `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239` trial-merged into the PR:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: passed, including 58 library tests and all integration suites. The new tests include 7 integration tests and 4 library tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The quick gate dry run completed. Its plan also includes changes from main since the PR branch point. I ran the full post crate suite for this review.
- No GitHub runner was used.

This is a safety review. I copied the unchanged kinematics module and its tests to a separate temporary crate. All 11 original tests passed there. I then ran two mutations myself:

- Set the held pole C angle to zero: the pole test failed with `expected modal 48.00000000000001, got 0`. I restored the source. The test passed.
- Removed the chord error split check: the chord test failed with `got 1` segment. I restored the source. The test passed.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Complete the clearance retract before C unwinds.** `crates/post/src/kinematics/path.rs:79`. The code emits one rapid move that both lifts the tool and changes C by a full turn. With default geometry, C travel of -450 to 450 degrees, and eleven 40-degree steps at a 40-degree tilt, C reaches -440 degrees. A marked retract from `[100,0,0]` to `[100,0,50]` then commands C from -440 to -80 degrees during the lift. At the joint midpoint, forward kinematics gives tip `[-100,0,25]`; the requested tip is `[100,0,25]`. The tool sweeps across the part before it reaches clearance. Keep C continuous through the lift. Permit the unwind only after clearance is established, with a checked path or a named refusal. Add a test that checks the retract path, not only its endpoint.

2. **[P1] Preserve machine pose continuity when the CL axis changes.** `crates/post/src/kinematics/path.rs:139`. Both path endpoints receive the new CL axis. When adjacent CL moves have different axes, `solve_path` solves a new start pose but emits no transition from the last end pose. A two-feed test at 40-degree tilt, with azimuths -90 and -50 degrees and a shared tip `[20,0,0]`, ends the first move at XYZ `[20,0,0]`, A=-40, C=0. The next move starts at XYZ `[15.320889,-9.848078,8.263518]`, A=-40, C=-40. No output move joins those poses. Emit and check the required orientation transition, or refuse the input by name. Add a test for adjacent moves with different axes.

3. **[P2] Refuse a path when a subdivision limit prevents the requested tolerance.** `crates/post/src/kinematics/path.rs:195`. At depth 14 the code stops checking the angular and chord limits and returns the segment as valid. A 40-to-60-degree tilt with `max_angular_step_deg=0.000001` returns 16,384 segments with a maximum A step of 0.001220703125 degrees. Check the limits at the depth cap and return a named error if they still fail. Apply the same rule to the 4,096-step cap in `emit_pole_c_reorient`. Add tests for both caps.

All three added local safety probes failed on the unchanged module. The PR worktree source was not edited. No evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the three findings from the latest review.

1. Clearance lifts keep C continuous and use checked subdivision. Later travel exhaustion returns a named refusal instead of an unchecked unwind. Pinned by `clearance_retract_keeps_c_continuous_and_checks_the_entire_lift` and the updated `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_travel_refusal`.
2. Adjacent moves with mismatched poses return `DiscontinuousPath`. Pinned by `adjacent_cl_axis_change_is_refused_instead_of_teleporting`.
3. Both subdivision caps return `SubdivisionLimitExceeded` when tolerance is unmet. Pinned by `continuous_subdivision_depth_cap_refuses_unmet_angular_tolerance`, `continuous_subdivision_depth_cap_refuses_unmet_chord_tolerance`, `pole_reorientation_step_cap_refuses_unmet_angular_tolerance`, and `pole_reorientation_step_cap_refuses_unmet_chord_tolerance`.

All six new pins failed under deliberate reversions and passed after restoration. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on this head.

Needs changes before merge.

The three earlier findings are fixed on this head. The clearance lift keeps C continuous. Adjacent pose gaps return `DiscontinuousPath`. Both subdivision limits return `SubdivisionLimitExceeded` when tolerance is not met. All six new safety tests pass.

Local results, with upstream/main `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239` merged into the review worktree without conflicts:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: passed. This includes 58 library tests, 7 AC inverse tests, 6 AC path safety tests, and all other post integration suites.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The quick gate dry run passed. Its plan includes changes from main since the branch point. The full post crate suite was run for this review.
- No GitHub runner was used. The PR changes no UI files, dependencies, or golden files.

This is a safety review. I copied the kinematics source and tests to a separate temporary crate. All 17 original tests passed there. I ran two mutations myself:

- Set held pole C to zero: the pole test failed with `expected modal 48.00000000000001, got 0`. I restored the source. The test passed.
- Removed the chord error split check: the chord test failed with `got 1` segment. I restored the source. The test passed.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Preserve arc geometry or refuse arc input.** `crates/post/src/kinematics/path.rs:132`. `solve_toolpath` copies each move into a straight `PathMove` and ignores `mv.arc`. With default machine settings, a 100 mm radius XY quarter-circle from `[100,0,0]` to `[0,100,0]`, centered at `[0,0]`, is accepted as one straight feed. Its midpoint is `[50,50,0]`, which is 29.289321881345245 mm inside the requested circle. This exceeds the 0.01 mm chord tolerance and can cut across the part. Convert arcs to checked chords within tolerance, or return a named error before solving an arc. Add a test for this input and for arcs in the other supported planes.

A local test of that arc failed on the unchanged source:

```text
arc accepted as 1 line(s); midpoint [50.0, 50.0, 0.0]; radial error 29.289321881345245 mm
```

The PR source was not edited. No evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the latest review finding. `solve_toolpath` now refuses CL arcs with `UnsupportedArc` and the source move index before solving. It cannot silently replace an arc with a straight cut.

Pinned by `cl_xy_quarter_circle_is_refused_instead_of_cutting_across_part`, `cl_xz_quarter_circle_is_refused_instead_of_cutting_across_part`, and `cl_yz_quarter_circle_is_refused_instead_of_cutting_across_part`. Each checks move indices 0 and 1. `cl_straight_feed_remains_supported` checks the straight-feed control.

Removing the refusal made all three arc pins fail. Restoring it made all 10 path safety tests pass. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The earlier findings are fixed on this head:

- Clearance lifts keep C continuous. Travel that requires an unchecked unwind is refused.
- Adjacent moves with different end and start poses return `DiscontinuousPath`.
- Both subdivision limits return `SubdivisionLimitExceeded` when the tolerance is not met.
- CL arcs return `UnsupportedArc` with the source move index. Tests cover XY, XZ, and YZ arcs at move indices 0 and 1. The straight feed test also passes.

This is a safety review of the new geometry and kinematics code. The PR changes no UI files, dependencies, or golden files. There are no changed golden lines to check.

Local results, with upstream/main `31f8d03d744e77ce707282d816e11efe0922f239` merged into the review worktree without conflicts:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 586 tests passed, with no failures. This includes 58 library tests, 7 AC inverse tests, and 10 AC path safety tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: passed. The plan includes changes from main since the branch point. I ran the full post crate suite for this review.
- No GitHub runner was used.

I copied the unchanged kinematics source and tests to a separate temporary crate. All 21 tests passed there. I ran these mutations myself:

1. Set held pole C to zero. The pole test failed: `expected modal 48.00000000000001, got 0`. After source restoration, the test passed.
2. Removed the chord error split check. The chord test failed: `expected 90-deg rotary sweep at >35mm radius to subdivide into many chords, got 1`. After source restoration, the test passed.
3. Removed the arc refusal. All three arc tests failed because the solver returned straight moves instead of `UnsupportedArc`. After source restoration, all three tests passed.

Requested before merge: none.

The PR source was not edited. No evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
